subtopic: IREE / Compiler-runtime separation and edge deployment
learningObjective: Understand why IREE separates compiler and runtime and how this enables edge and cross-target deployment.
stem: Which statement best captures the reason IREE cleanly separates its compiler and runtime?

options.text: The separation is purely for internal code organization; end users must run both the compiler and the runtime on the target device at every model invocation, since IREE bytecode cannot be executed without the compiler.
The runtime is only used for testing during development; production deployments must re-implement the runtime themselves because IREE does not distribute a production runtime binary.

The compiler is a heavyweight AOT tool that produces a compact, self-describing artifact; the runtime is a small embeddable library that can be linked into edge/mobile apps without shipping the full MLIR toolchain, enabling deployment where the target device lacks the resources or licensing to host a full compiler.
IREE compiler and runtime share the same binary at deployment; the 'compiler-runtime separation' is a marketing term and has no impact on the artifact structure or edge deployment story.

explanation: IREE separates a heavyweight AOT compiler (which needs the full MLIR toolchain, LLVM, target libraries, etc.) from a lightweight runtime library that executes the compiled `.vmfb` bytecode. This lets edge/mobile deployments ship only the runtime + compiled artifact, without needing to host the compiler on-device. This mirrors the general 'compile once, deploy many' philosophy of AOT toolchains and is central to IREE's edge story.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: compiled artifacts do not need the compiler at runtime.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: IREE distributes production-ready runtime libraries.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: AOT + slim runtime enables edge deployment.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: the separation is real and structural.

assumptions: IREE deployment model as documented on iree.dev.
nonImplications: Does not imply the compiler cannot be embedded (it can, for JIT flows).
Does not imply the runtime is single-purpose; it is used server-side too.

distractorRationales.A: Wrong claim that runtime requires compiler.
distractorRationales.B: Wrong claim that runtime is dev-only.
